The per-kind payload stored in ``environments.config``.

Every field is optional at the type level and REQUIRED-BY-KIND at the
validator level, the same shape ``InteractiveIterationDetails`` uses for its
platform↔field coupling. ``extra="forbid"``: a silently-ignored config key is
a customer debugging a target that was never set.

EnvironmentDescriptor.description:
An ad-hoc environment, described inline on the session that uses it.

Also the shape of the FROZEN SNAPSHOT a session carries after it was opened
against a REGISTERED environment (``environment_id``), which is why the field
is still named ``platform``: it holds the environment's ``kind``, and renaming a
live public field to match the newer internal vocabulary would break clients
for no behavioural gain.

platform.description: The kind of surface (e.g. `web`, `device`, `world`). Open union: new values may be added over time; clients must tolerate unknown values rather than failing on them.
platform.title: Platform

EnvironmentDescriptor.title: EnvironmentDescriptor

EnvironmentKind.description:
What KIND of surface a registered environment is (ADR-0026).

Deliberately NOT called "platform": four incompatible platform vocabularies
already exist (``InteractiveIterationDetails.platform`` =
browser/android/ios/figma/code, ``FrameSourceType``, ``DEVICE_PLATFORMS``,
and the session lane's own free string) and they share no member. ``kind`` is
the one closed vocabulary the environment object owns; the lane-local ones
are mapped at their boundaries, never merged.

The member set is the session lane's MEASURED usage (dev ``agent_sessions``
holds exactly ``web``, ``device``, ``world``; the old ``EnvironmentDescriptor``
docstring's "game" is ``world``). It is GROWABLE and stored as a VARCHAR, not
a Postgres enum: adding a kind must not need an ``ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE``
(which also forces a new staging boundary in
``scripts/test_db/upgrade_stages.sh``). Same posture as ``ApiKeyScope``.

Closed on the WRITE path (the request DTO parses through this enum), OPEN on
the READ path (responses type ``kind`` as ``str``): a row written by a newer
server carrying an unknown kind must still read back rather than fail
validation. That asymmetry IS the open-union contract the public DTOs
document via ``_OPEN_UNION_NOTE``.
EnvironmentKind.title: EnvironmentKind

(the measured ceiling is a handful per workspace, not a stream), so a cursor
would be ceremony. If that stops being true this grows the same keyset shape
the session list uses.

UpdateEnvironmentRequest.description:
Partial update: an omitted field is left alone.

``None`` is a real value for the three nullable fields (it clears them), so
"omitted" and "explicitly null" must stay distinguishable — the router reads
``model_fields_set`` rather than testing for None. ``kind`` is updatable but
re-validates the config against the NEW kind, so a web→device switch that
leaves only a ``url`` behind is a 422 rather than a broken row.

bearerAuth.description: Workspace API key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer ish_sk_live_...`. Keys are workspace-scoped machine principals minted in Settings > Developers (shown once at mint). Scopes: `sessions:run` (create a session, submit turns, close), `sessions:read` (read the session and trace), `environments:read` and `environments:write` (manage the workspace's registered environments). A key is minted with the two `sessions:*` scopes by default; the `environments:*` pair must be requested. An ish user access token also works on the same header for personal scripts.

info.description:
The ish Developer API: the entry point for getting human feedback on whatever you're building, in whichever format you need.

Its first surface is **sessions**: you open a session for one of your personas inside *your own* environment, submit what the persona perceives (human-sensory observations: a rendered screen, an error message) along with the set of actions your environment currently offers, and the persona decides one action per turn and tells you how it felt. Your code executes the chosen action and loops. The environment loop is decide-only; ish never locates or executes anything in your environment (see ADR-0020/0021).

## Vocabulary

The public vocabulary is **workspace**, **persona**, **environment**, and **session**, and the wire uses these names directly:

- `workspace_id`: the workspace that owns the persona and is billed for the   session (the create path is `/workspaces/{workspace_id}/sessions`).
- `persona_id`: the persona the session drives.
- `environment_id`: a registered environment in that workspace — a named target   with its own operating notes and default action vocabulary. Register one and   reference it, or describe an ad-hoc one inline on the session; supply exactly   one of the two.

**"Session" here means one API session: a single persona working toward one goal in your environment, turn by turn.** It is not the ish product's notion of a study session (a person sitting down with a study), and it is unrelated to a browser session. Sessions live under `/v1/sessions`.

## Authentication

All requests use a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is a **workspace API key** (prefix `ish_sk_live_`), a workspace-scoped machine principal minted in Settings > Developers and shown exactly once at mint. Scopes: `sessions:run` (create, submit turns, close), `sessions:read` (read the session and trace), and `environments:read` / `environments:write` for the environment registry. Keys are minted with the two `sessions:*` scopes; ask for `environments:*` explicitly. An ish user access token (JWT) also works on the same header for personal scripts; server integrations should use keys.

## Versioning & forward-compatibility

The API is versioned in the URL path (`/api/v1`). Several enum-typed and block-typed fields are **open unions**: new values may be added over time, and clients MUST tolerate values they do not recognize rather than failing on them. The field descriptions call these out.

## Correlation & errors

Every response carries an **`X-Request-Id`** header; quote it in support requests. Error responses additionally echo it in the body as `request_id`.

Two error-body shapes exist; parse defensively, they differ:

- **`ValidationError`**: the request-validation layer (HTTP 422): a malformed   body (wrong types, missing fields, an invalid observation `type`, a bad enum   value, `parameters` that don't fit the model). A field-level envelope   (`error_code`, `errors[]`, `suggestions[]`; `suggestions` is CLI-oriented   boilerplate; ignore it for API use).
- **`Error`**: everything else, a `{ detail, request_id }` envelope. This   covers the handler layer's business-rule 422s (e.g. `exactly one image   observation block is required`; `persona has no renderable background`) as well   as 401 / 403 / 404 / 409 / 502. `detail` may be a structured object carrying a   machine-readable `error_kind` (e.g. `idempotency_conflict`,   `turn_index_mismatch`, `decision_invalid`).

That is why 422 is documented on the responses below as either shape (`oneOf`).

delete.description:
Delete an environment.

A hard delete, not an archive: sessions that ran here keep their frozen
name/kind snapshot and their ``environment_id`` is SET NULL, so nothing in the
decision trace is lost. Archive-vs-delete is therefore a UX question, not a
data-integrity one, and pre-launch the cheap answer wins (ADR-0026).

List a workspace's sessions, newest first (keyset-paginated).

Ordered ``created_at DESC, id DESC``. Page forward with ``after`` set to the
prior response's ``next_cursor``; ``has_more`` signals another page. Each row
is a summary (status, goal, environment, persona, turn counts, key
attribution, accrued credits, timestamps) — the per-turn decision trace lives
on the detail GET.

post.description:
Open a decide-only session for a workspace/platform persona.

Supports the standard ``Idempotency-Key`` header: a retry with the same key
and body replays the existing session (200 instead of 201); the same key
with a different body is a 409 ``idempotency_conflict``.
